messages.subject: Stacked Bar Plot Question
parts:
I have the following code that used to produce a stacked bar plot with
no issues. Recently...I have begun to see an error that I am not sure
how to resolve.

I have two data frames:
uptime (http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/uptime.csv)
uptimemerge (http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/uptimemerge.csv)

I have used the following code with great success in the past but now
displays the following error:

x11(width=7.0,height=4.0)
d = ggplot(uptimemerge,aes(x=Date,y=RunTime,fill=timeType)) +
geom_bar(width=0.8,colour="black") +
geom_text(aes(label=RunTime),data=uptime,size=3,angle=90,hjust=1.5) +
facet_wrap(~Machine,)
d + scale_fill_manual(name="Status",value=c("yellowgreen","grey60")) +
ylim(0,100) +
labs(x="", y="%Time Spent Synthesizing") +
geom_hline(yintercept=85,colour="red",linetype=2) +
opts(title=paste("Run Time Summary") +
opts(legend.position="none") +
opts(plot.title=theme_text(size=10)) +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=90,hjust=1,size=8)) +
opts(axis.title.y=theme_text(angle=90,size=9)) +
opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(size=9))

Error in if (!is.null(data$ymin) && !all(data$ymin == 0))
warning("Stacking not well defined when ymin != 0", :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Can anyone fill me in on why this is occurring?

messages.author: 28f7cf43544f2467
messages.subject: Re: Stacked Bar Plot Question
parts:
So after looking into this problem some more...it turns out that the
issue lies with duplicate records in my data.

For some reason...the SP that returns this data had inserted two
records for the same date and machine (2010-07-09 Phobos). The
stacking issue must have arisen due to this data anomaly and now makes
perfect sense.

> opts(axis.title.y=theme_text(angle=90,size=9)) +
> opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(size=9))

> Error in if (!is.null(data$ymin) && !all(data$ymin == 0))
> warning("Stacking not well defined when ymin != 0",  :
>   missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
>
> Can anyone fill me in on why this is occurring?

Short answer:

Since you have pre-summarized data, you need to add stat="identity" to
the geom_bar.

Long answer:

It helps, both for others figuring out what is wrong and for you
discovering solutions on your own, to make the example both completely
reproducible and minimal. For example, in defining the data.frames:

uptimemerge <- read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/
uptimemerge.csv")

Since read.csv can take a URL, this is easy to do. Also, it makes
sure that everyone is working with the same set of data. For example,
doing this gives Date as a factor. Was it a factor in your original
data.frame? Or was it at Date or POSIXct or POSIXlt? Maybe it
doesn't matter, maybe it does. But it is one more thing that might
vary that may be related to the problem.

Second, make the example minimal. You don't use uptime in your
example, so get rid of it entirely. Start trimming out parts of the
plot call and see if the error stays. I cut out the ops, labs, and
ylim parts and the error was still there. Then I took out the custom
fill scale and the error was still there. Then I took out the
geom_line and geom_text and the error was still there. Same with the
faceting. I could even take out the width and colour arguments to
geom_bar and still have the error. Anything else I took out changed
the error. So the minimal reproducible example is now:

uptimemerge <- read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/
uptimemerge.csv")

ggplot(uptimemerge, aes(x=Date, y=RunTime, fill=timeType)) +
geom_bar()

If I take out the fill=timeType, the error changes to "Error in
pmin(y, 0) : object 'y' not found" That doesn't really make any more
sense than the first error, but at least tells me that the fill is
important to getting the error I see.

If I take out the y=RunTime (putting the fill back in), I get a plot!
Not the plot I want or expect, but a plot.Certainly one that does not
incorporate the RunTime in any way.

By this point (if not sooner), I'd be heading to the geom_bar
documentation: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html
There, it describes geom_bar as, by default, summarizing 1 dimensional
data into counts. Also, it has the highlighted comment: "Advice: If
you have presummarised data, use stat="identity" to turn off the
default summary" which is the case you have here.

To make the minimal example work, add stat="identity" to the geom_bar
call:

ggplot(uptimemerge, aes(x=Date, y=RunTime, fill=timeType)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity")

From here, you can go back and make the same change to your more
complicated version, and see if it works there.

--
Brian Diggs
Senior Research Associate
Oregon Health & Science University

parts:
Thanks for the reply Brian and your posting tips are duly noted.

For clarification...the second data.frame (uptime) is used in the
example to display text on the chart...but going back to your original
point...it isn't completely necessary for the reproduction of the
problem.

I did follow the same progressive approach as you describe. Use of
stat="identity" produced a chart similar to what I was expecting but
something was still wrong. Bars were being stacked that should not be.
It wasn't until I looked a bit closer that I realized the problem
potentially had something to do with duplicate records.
